keyframe_review.note: 305,359 km2 covering all of Tamil Nadu, 79% of Kerala and part of Karnataka, taken from Cliopatria's Early Chera, Chola and Pandya rows, which end in 305. The Pallava page has the Pallavas 'dominated the southern Telugu region and the northern parts of the Tamil region', Skandavarman's dominions from the Krishna to the Pennar; the Kalabhra page puts the Kalabhras 'after the ancient dynasties of the early Cholas, the early Pandyas and Chera', with the Kalabhras not in power near the Penner and Vellar rivers in Skandavarman's day. Nothing opened gives the Pallavas the Tamil heartland or Kerala. The core of 275-305 is used instead until the Cholas take Kanchi (353).

24,117 km2 (Rayalaseema, 77.8-79.5E, 13.7-15.9N), without Kanchi: this fits the Pallava page ('The Cholas drove the Pallavas away from Kanchi in the mid-4th century, in the reign of Vishnugopa', chronology 350-355) and its 'southern Telugu region'. The Gupta shape takes 116 cells of the old Pallava coast in 353 (Samudragupta's southern campaign). Boundaries are not given by the page (unverified: page budget).

37,874 km2, 140 cells in Andhra Pradesh. The Kalabhra page: the Pallavas were once their overlords and the Kalabhras ruled the Tamil country between the 3rd and 6th centuries; the Pallava page has the 'political convulsion' of the Kalabhra invasion of the Tamil country under Vishnugopavarman II (c. 500-525). No page gives the Pallava frontier of 451-554; the shape stands as the southern Telugu remnant (unverified: page budget).

Years only: the shape holds 555-574. Kalabhra page: Simhavishnu 'consolidated his kingdom up to the Kaveri river by c. 575 CE'; Pallava page: 'Towards the close of the 6th century, the Pallava Simhavishnu stuck a blow against the Kalabhras'. See late-pallava-empire_575.

New keyframe 806-897: Cliopatria's Pallava row ends in 805 but the Pallava page has Dantivarman (795-846), Nandivarman III (846-869) and Aparajitavarman (879-897), 'Disestablished: 897', and the dynasty 'finally defeated by the Chola ruler Aditya I in the 9th century'. The 805 shape is carried unchanged. Cliopatria's Rashtrakuta shapes of 806-897 overlap 184 of its 387 cells (Andhra interior), the Chola shape of 898 overlaps 131: the Rashtrakuta group (sa-03) must decide whether that is Rashtrakuta overlordship; nothing opened supports it. fx-34 (F330): decided: the rashtrakuta-dynasty keyframes 806, 819, 825, 840, 850 and 860 now subtract this shape (the Pallava page: 'dominated the southern Telugu region and the northern parts of the Tamil region'; the Rashtrakuta page has no holding there), so the 184-cell overlap is gone.

Samudragupta page: he defeated Vishnugopa of Kanchi and the kings of Pishtapura, Kottura, Vengi, Palakka (Ugrasena, possibly a Pallava viceroyalty) and Devarashtra, listed as captured and then released. Cliopatria's Gupta shape of 353 takes 116 cells of its old Pallava shape, 74 of them inside this core. The year is Cliopatria's; the Pallava page does not mention the defeat.

region.text: Kanchi and the Tamil country up to the Kaveri, from the Kalabhras

ledger.note: c. 575: Simhavishnu takes the Tamil country up to the Kaveri from the Kalabhras. Kalabhra page: Simhavishnu 'consolidated his kingdom up to the Kaveri river by c. 575 CE' and the Kalabhra rule 'had ended for certain by the last quarter of 6th century'; Simhavishnu page: he 'overthrew the Kalabhras and conquered the region up to the Kaveri River' and 'He was the first Pallava monarch whose domain extended beyond Kanchipuram (Kanchi) to the south'. The Pallava page dates his accession 537-615 depending on the list. Cliopatria draws the gain in 602.

ledger.note: c. 602: the northern provinces go to the Chalukyas. Mahendravarman I page: 'the Chalukya monarch Pulakeshin II attacked the Pallava realm'; 'The Pallavas fought a series of wars in the northern Vengi region' and 'Although Mahendravarman saved his capital, he lost the northern provinces to Pulakeshin.' Pullalur is not dated on the page. Cliopatria's Pallava shape loses 75 cells to the Chalukya row of 602 (Rayalaseema).

notes:
Cliopatria row: one row, 283-805; the dossier extends it to 897 (Pallava page, infobox 'Disestablished: 897'), carrying the 805 shape unchanged for 806-897, and starts it at 275.
Page budget: 5 of 5 on the Pallava pages (Pallava dynasty, Simhavishnu, Mahendravarman I, Kalabhra dynasty, Narasimhavarman I); the Samudragupta and Mayurasharma pages (opened for other dossiers) are cited for the Gupta campaign and the Kadamba war.
The 306-352 Cliopatria shape is marked wrong: it gives the Pallavas all of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and part of Karnataka, land that Cliopatria's Early Chera, Chola and Pandya rows (ending 305) and the Kalabhra row (from 353) cover, and that no page opened gives to the Pallavas. The corrected keyframes keep the Telugu coast and Kanchi until the Chola expulsion c. 353.
Unsettled: (1) the dates of Simhavishnu (555-590, 575-600, 575-615, 537-570 on the pages); the 575 start of the Tamil expansion rests on the Kalabhra page's 'by c. 575'; (2) the Pallava frontier in 353-574 (the pages say only that the Cholas took Kanchi and the Kalabhras ruled the Tamil country); (3) the 602 loss to the Chalukyas: the pages date no part of the Chalukya war except 642; (4) Cliopatria's Rashtrakuta shapes overlap the Pallava 805 shape in 806-897 (184 cells), and the Chola shape in 898-935 (131 cells); (5) Pallava rule over Vatapi after 642 is not on the pages; (6) the page's ruler lists differ (several 'other lists'): the first list is used and gaps (300-350, 355-575, 722-732, 869-879) are left open.
Gazetteer names needed: Tondaimandalam (region: northern Tamil Nadu around Kanchipuram), used here only as a Kanchipuram radius.
